Isotopes of the same element have the same **mass number**.
cards.back_md:

back_blocks.md: Isotopes are named using the **chemical symbol** (or element name) followed by a dash and the **mass number**. For example, carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon with 6 and 8 neutrons respectively.

front_blocks.md: Why do **isotopes** of the same element have identical **chemical** properties?

back_blocks.md: Isotopes have the same number of **electrons** and the same **electron configuration**. Because chemical behaviour is determined by **electrons** (especially those in the outer shell), all isotopes of an element react in the same way.

front_blocks.md: Isotopes of the same element have the same **density**.

back_blocks.md: Isotopes have different numbers of **neutrons**, so they have different **masses**. This leads to differences in **density** and **relative atomic mass**, even though their chemical properties are identical.

Isotopes of the same element have the same **density**.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Isotopes have different numbers of **neutrons**, so they have different **masses**. This leads to differences in **density** and **relative atomic mass**, even though their chemical properties are identical.

front_blocks.md: Why do **isotopes** of the same element differ in **physical** properties?

back_blocks.md: Isotopes differ in the number of **neutrons**, which changes the nuclear **mass** without affecting charge. This leads to different **relative atomic masses**, **densities** and behaviour in processes such as **mass spectrometry**.

front_blocks.md: Carbon-14 has an atomic number of 6 and mass number 14. How many **protons**, **neutrons** and **electrons** does a neutral carbon-14 atom have?

back_blocks.md:
1. **Protons:** 6 (= atomic number)
2. **Neutrons:** 8 (= 14 − 6)
3. **Electrons:** 6 (neutral atom, so electrons = protons)

cards.front_md: Carbon-14 has an atomic number of 6 and mass number 14. How many **protons**, **neutrons** and **electrons** does a neutral carbon-14 atom have?
cards.back_md:
A neutral **carbon-14** atom has:

1. **Protons:** 6 (= atomic number)
2. **Neutrons:** 8 (= 14 − 6)
3. **Electrons:** 6 (neutral atom, so electrons = protons)
